Results are stored in the session with the server URL and the radio values of the same seconds. A test during a traffic capture is flagged, because the capture slows it down.
The main target. Use a server you control, so results stay comparable between tests and days. For a LibreSpeed server, enter its address and tap Fill; any other web server works with three URLs.
Answers small requests quickly, e.g. an empty page.
Serves a large file (tens of MB or more); requested again until the time is up.

Optional, for comparison only. Adds a second button on the Live screen that tests against %1$s. Not your server and never the default: the result depends on Cloudflare\'s nearest site and its route, and many large tests in a row are blocked for a while (HTTP 429). Each result stores the URL it used.
Start and stop it on the Live screen while a session is logging. One capture per session; it stops when the session stops.
NetLogger runs its own VPN on the phone. Android asks you once to allow it. Only one VPN can run at a time, so turn off any other VPN first.

It records the IP traffic between each app and the VPN, and which app owns each connection. It does not see radio signalling, and packet sizes and timing are rebuilt by the VPN, not the ones on the air.
The session export adds capture.pcap (open it in Wireshark), capture_sync.csv (clock alignment with the radio log) and connections.csv (the app of each connection).
Files grow with the traffic: a speed test during a capture adds about 100 MB to the pcap. Speed tests during a capture are flagged, because the capture slows them down.
Applies to the next capture. Traffic of apps not chosen bypasses the VPN and is not recorded.
Everything the phone sends and receives, including background apps and system services.
Only the apps you tick below, e.g. one video app for a QoE test. Smaller files that are easier to analyse.
No app selected yet: until you tick one, all apps are captured.
Only apps with an icon in the app drawer are listed. Include NetLogger itself to capture its speed tests.
The largest packet the VPN passes on. Applies to the next capture; the value is stored with it.
The same packet sizes as on a mobile network, so the pcap looks like real traffic. Fast links lose up to a quarter of their download speed during the capture.
Hardly slows the phone down (about 3 percent), but packets are bigger than on the air. Use it when throughput matters more than packet sizes.
